quotes.text: We must meet the moment, slow down development, and recognize that these growing risks and dangers demand urgent, bipartisan collaboration and international coordination. This concerted effort is essential to ensure that this technology develops in a way that’s safe, secure, and benefits everyone.

I strongly support an independent federal review and testing process for the most powerful AI models before they are released, along with enforceable safety standards, incident-reporting requirements, regular audits, and strong protections for employees who report dangers or violations.

I share the alarm of many Mainers about the community and environmental impacts of data centers including emissions, water usage, air pollution, noise pollution, and PFAS and other contaminants and worry about their long-term health effects on nearby residents.

AI’s most serious risks do not stop at national borders. The United States must work with allies, competitors, and adversaries to establish shared safety standards, prevent dangerous uses, and slow the international race to deploy increasingly powerful systems without adequate safeguards.
Since these technologies were created using our collective labor, knowledge, and creativity, technology companies will have to pay up for the economic and social disruption they inflict.

On Tuesday, the President revoked Biden-era vehicle pollution and fuel economy standards.

Why? He thinks too many EVs will strain the electric grid. 

Meanwhile, he wants to invest half-a-*trillion* dollars in AI, which will require far more energy than meeting EV goals. (1/2)

Mr. President, there’s people that are dying.

Millions of Americans are worried about losing their health care, affording groceries, and keeping a roof over their heads.

Our friends and neighbors are enduring abuses and inhumane treatment at the hands of ICE.

Innocent civilians, including children, are dying by the thousands in Gaza.

Ukrainians are defending their country and sovereignty against Russia.

Our servicemembers, including those suffering aboard the USS Lincoln, are being put in harm’s way to fight an illegal war in the Middle East that nobody asked for.

And this is what the President is spending his time on? Childish AI slop bullying our closest neighbor and ally.

Get a grip.

we're hearing so much frightening news about how AI is acting on its own and how little regulation there's been. And Congress often follows the technology companies. We've seen that with social media and other things.

This is one of the biggest challenges of our time. [...] I think it's our responsibility to think about at a national level how do we make sure that we rein in you know what sometimes is talked about is the total whole destruction of humanity, but also in the shorter version how will it impact jobs and which jobs and how will we deal with that?
